headline: Approved posters for Know Your Vote and teen-violence seminars; agreed to invite police chief to October 8 meeting.
summary: The commission reviewed Old Business items, including Canopy's Title IX position and plans for fall seminars. It approved the June 11, 2026 minutes and agreed to invite Chief Reynolds to the October 8 meeting.

Unanimously preferred Tatiana's personal story for the November 17 Immigration Presentation; confirmation is pending.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Human Rights & Relations Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, August 13, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
Third Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 Chair, Claudia LeSueur, called the meeting to order at approximately 7:11 PM, seconded 
by Commissioner, Tiffany Artist Wilson.  
  
2. ATTENDANCE   
 The role was taken by B & C, Clerk, Porsche Edmundson.  
Present: Commissioners: Claudia LeSueur, Chair; Tiffany Artist Wilson; Dana Parmelee 
Guzman; Ganiyu s. Mimiko and Gopika Sheth, Youth Representative.  
Porsche Edmundson 
 
  
3. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 The Commission confirmed that its official email address, HBC_humanRR@hamden.com, 
is now fully functional. Upon gaining access, Clerk Edmundson noted that there were 
approximately one year's worth of administrative emails, most of which were 
interdepartmental and administrative in nature. No new public correspondence was 
received beyond the three previously discussed.  
  
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 Commissioners discussed clarifying language in prior minutes to ensure accuracy and 
transparency. Under Old Business, the phrase “pursue a July meeting” was corrected to 
“pursue a meeting”, as the Commission was not planning to invite Chief Reynolds to a July 
meeting. Under Community Education Seminars, the phrase “secure September dates” 
was revised to reflect autumn dates, since the Commission intended to schedule seminars 
broadly in the fall, not exclusively in September.  
Commissioners agreed that future minutes should be written in a narrative format rather 
than bullet points, allowing the public to clearly understand the discussions and decisions 
made.  
Action Items: Minutes from June 11, 2026, were approved. July minutes will be reviewed 
and approved in September once edits are complete.  
 
  
5. REPORTS
The Mayor’s Office reported that one new application for a regular commissioner position 
was received in May. Two applications previously mentioned from autumn were not 
located. The new applicant has been approved by the Mayor’s Office and will be forwarded 
to the Legislative Council for final approval in early September. Youth Commissioners will 
also be reappointed at the first September Legislative Council meeting.  
Commissioners agreed to continue posting updates on social media and distributing 
posters to encourage district-wide engagement and attract new applicants.  
 
 
  
6. CORRESPONDENCE 
The Commission confirmed that its official email address, HBC_humanRR@hamden.com, 
is now fully functional. Upon gaining access, Clerk Edmundson noted that there were 
approximately four to five years of administrative emails, most of which were 
interdepartmental and administrative in nature. No new public correspondence was 
received beyond the three previously discussed.   
 The Commission confirmed that its official email address, HBC_humanRR@hamden.com, 
is now fully functional. Upon gaining access, Clerk Edmundson noted that there were 
approximately four to five years of administrative emails, most of which were 
interdepartmental and administrative in nature. No new public correspondence was 
received beyond the three previously discussed.  
  
7. OLD BUSINESS   
 The Commission reviewed Canopy’s Title IX position and agreed to monitor ongoing 
developments rather than take immediate action. Legal constraints may limit Canopy’s 
ability to comment publicly during active proceedings. This item will remain under Old 
Business monthly to demonstrate continued awareness and allow public comment.  
No commissioners attended the Newhall Ville meeting held on July 23. Attempts to locate 
notes or recordings were unsuccessful. Commissioners will reach out to Member of council 
Rhonda Caldwell for updates, as she has previously livestreamed these meetings.  
Commissioners attempted to register for participation in National Night Out on August 4 but 
received no response from organizers. Only one email bounced back as inactive. The 
Commission will follow up with the Hamden Police Department next year to ensure 
participation.  
 
The ACLU confirmed participation in the September 22 “Know Your Vote” presentation. 
Posters were reviewed and approved with minor grammar adjustments. Commissioners 
will distribute posters at coffee shops, grocery stores, Town Hall, and online. Refreshments 
will be provided by commissioners.  
The October 20 “Preventing Teen Violence” seminar poster layout was approved. The 
target audience includes teachers, principals, social workers, police, and youth-serving 
professionals. Commissioners expect strong attendance and may schedule a follow-up 
session in spring if demand is high.  
For the November 17 “Immigration Presentation,” two options were discussed: a general 
legal services presentation by New Haven Legal Assistance or a personal narrative by 
Tatiana from IRIS about emigrating from Ukraine and her path to citizenship. 
Commissioners unanimously preferred Tatiana’s personal story for the November 
presentation. Confirmation is pending.
8. NEW BUSINESS   
 The Chief of Police’s office offered dates in September or October for attendance. 
Commissioners agreed to invite Chief Reynolds to the October 8 meeting, aligning with the 
October 20 teen-violence seminar. If unavailable, a representative will be requested.  
 Additional Updates  
Commissioners noted that updates regarding Newhall Ville appeared in the New Haven 
Register. Members will share any relevant articles to stay informed.  
 
  
9. ADJOURNMENT   
 The meeting adjourned at 8:15 PM.  
Minutes Prepared By:  
B & C, Clerk, Porsche Edmundson  
 Human Rights & Relations Commission Town of Hamden  
 
A recording of this meeting is available via the official Town of Hamden Boards & 
Commissions portal.
